answer: Stop sybils with proof-of-storage commitment: every identity must hold unique data. First, a new agent locks 500 GB of encrypted data on its disk for 180 days and posts the storage root. Second, each epoch it must return 20 random chunks within 30 seconds; a miss burns its 300 POA bond. Third, one disk cannot hold ten thousand 500 GB vaults. 10,000 fakes need 5 petabytes of disks, $1,200,000 in hardware, and 3,000,000 POA in bonds. Like a glacier, honest storage moves slow, while a zephyr of fakes melts away - the kernel of trust is data you actually keep.
